newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore dollar hit by fresh ringgit/Sing buying.
newsitem.headline: Singapore dollar hit by fresh ringgit/Sing buying.

text.p: The Singapore dollar weakened further against its U.S. counterpart in late Asian trade on Tuesday as the Malaysian ringgit breached a two-and-a-half year high against the Singapore dollar, dealers said.
"There was fresh buying of ringgit/Sing this afternoon. When it broke the 0.5800 level, there were stops from 0.5805/10 right up to 0.5820/25," said a Japanese bank dealer.
He said the ringgit/Sing cross hit a high of 0.5812 but profit-taking interest by U.S. hedge funds kept it from climbing further. It was quoted at 0.5808/14 after the Asian close.
The Singapore dollar fell through a recent support area around the 1.4360/70 level on the back of the ringgit/Sing buying. It was quoted at 1.4370/80.
The dealer said the ringgit/Sing cross would face near-term resistance at 0.5840 but added, "In the longer term, I think 60 cents is fairly good value."

He said the Singapore dollar was likely to slide gradually to 1.4500 versus the U.S. unit but added that it would be protected around 1.4380 for the time being. "Each time it gets down there, I think there's some genuine (U.S. dollar) selling interest," he said.
A Malaysian bank dealer said Tuesday's ringgit/Sing buying was driven by London- and Hong Kong-based funds going into the cross for its yield.
A U.S. bank dealer in Singapore said the U.S. dollar faced little serious resistance on its way to a target of S$1.4500.
"But the most likely scenario is that we'll see a 40-point move up, a 20-point move down and then consolidate, followed by another 40-point move up," he added.
